jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Missouri, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Missouri, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Missouri Senate, Missouri House and U.S. House districts, county commissions, townships, cities, towns and villages, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: Missouri district map, what district am I in, Missouri Senate district, Missouri House district, Missouri congressional district, Missouri county commission, Missouri township, Missouri school district lookup

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Missouri, and who represents you there.

head.title: Missouri district lookup — districtry Missouri
head.description: Tap the map or search a Missouri address: county, Missouri Senate, Missouri House and U.S. House districts — and who represents you.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Missouri, and who holds it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 8 congressional districts — the largest districts Missouri carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 8 features for Missouri, measured 2026-10-21. LAYER 4 AND NOT LAYER 0, AND IT STAYS LAYER 4 AFTER 3 JANUARY 2027: layer 0 already carries the map the General Assembly passed in 2025, which a referendum on the 3 November 2026 ballot has held back, and the U.S. Supreme Court's order of 25 September 2026 kept the 2022 map for the 2026 election, so the members elected in 2026 are elected from the 2022 map. Layer 4 is that map, and it matches the state's own map of the current congressional districts district for district; layer 0 would grow the 5th District from about 1,118 km2 to about 21,546 km2. If voters keep the 2025 map, it first applies to the 2028 election. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Missouri Senate District
layers.rank_note: 34 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Missouri Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: Missouri Office of Administration — State Senate Boundaries, the state's own map of the Senate districts of the plan filed in 2022, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 34 features, measured 2026-10-21. THE STATE'S OWN MAP AND NOT THE CENSUS BUREAU'S: measured against the plan's own filed map, the state's map puts 99.998% of the state's area in the same district, and every district is at least 99.95% the same ground; the Census Bureau's copy goes as low as 99.08% the same ground, in Senate District 13. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: mo-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Missouri Senate's own pages for each senator: the name, the party, and the Capitol office's room and telephone, with each senator's e-mail address from the Secretary of State's roster of the General Assembly. A vacant seat carries a record saying so.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 115 counties (114 counties and the independent City of St. Louis), pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, who sits on its county commission or county council (with its county executive where the county elects one), and who holds its other elected county offices.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 115 features (114 counties and the City of St. Louis, which belongs to no county), measured 2026-10-21. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: mo-county-officials.json, rebuilt weekly from the Missouri Secretary of State's Missouri Roster, the 2025-2026 edition printed in June 2025: the presiding commissioner and district commissioners of each of the 110 counties governed by a county commission, the county executive and the council or legislature of the four charter counties, the City of St. Louis's mayor and the president of its Board of Aldermen, and each county's other elected officers (clerk, assessor, collector, treasurer, recorder, circuit clerk, prosecuting attorney, sheriff, coroner, public administrator, surveyor), with the telephone and e-mail address the roster prints beside that official alone. Jackson County's county executive, recalled after the roster was printed, is not named. The card says which edition it read, and names nobody it does not print.

layers.label: Missouri House District
layers.rank_note: 163 House districts — smaller on average than a county, larger than a school district

source.answers: The Missouri House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: Missouri Office of Administration — State House Boundaries, the state's own map of the House districts of the plan filed in 2022, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 163 features, measured 2026-10-21. THE STATE'S OWN MAP AND NOT THE CENSUS BUREAU'S: measured against the plan's own filed map, the state's map puts 99.995% of the state's area in the same district, and every district is at least 99.85% the same ground; the Census Bureau's copy goes as low as 97.33% the same ground, in House District 135, and puts about 1.45 km2 of Springfield in House District 135 where the plan and the state's map put it in 131. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: mo-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Missouri House's own published list of members: the name, the party, and the Capitol office's room, telephone and e-mail address. The list also prints each member's home town, which is not read. A vacant seat carries a record saying so.

layers.label: County Commission District
layers.rank_note: Two commission districts per county, about 780 km2 of land on average against about 1,090 km2 for a Missouri House district; drawn only in the 36 counties whose county map viewer, download, posted township map, GIS office or clerk publishes or sends them

source.answers: The county commission district covering the point, and the district commissioner elected from it, in the 36 counties where this app draws the lines. The layer is hidden in the other counties, where the County card still names both district commissioners and the presiding commissioner.

boundary.label: Integrity GIS county map viewers — the commission district layer each county's own public map viewer carries, for Barton, Bates, Buchanan, Camden, Chariton, Christian, Cooper, Dade, DeKalb, Lincoln, Maries, Marion, McDonald, Miller, Phelps, Polk, Pulaski, Ralls, Ray, Vernon and Warren counties, read 2026-10-23. Each answers exactly two districts, whose names match the seats the Secretary of State's Missouri Roster lists for that county. Clipped to the Census Bureau's county line, with the few slivers the viewer leaves between its two districts given to the district beside them. Whether each viewer's line is the one the county's elections use today is NOT established: no viewer gives a date for its lines, and Missouri law sets no date by which a county must redraw them.

Cole County — the commission district shapefile MidMO GIS, the map site of the City of Jefferson and Cole County, publishes for download (CC_Commissioner.zip), created 11 May 2011, clipped to the Census Bureau's county line in the same way. Whether it is the line the county's elections use today is not established either.

Lawrence County — the county's posted map of its two commission districts (a 2024 scan), whose Eastern District is outlined around six whole townships: Aurora, Buck Prairie, Freistatt, Ozark, Spring River and Turnback. Drawn as the union of those townships' Census Bureau (TIGER) lines, clipped to the county line in the same way; the county clerk pointed to that map when asked on 2026-10-23. Whether it is the line the county's elections use today is not established either.

Cass County — the shapefile of its two commission districts that Cass County GIS, in the Assessor's office, e-mailed to this project on 23 October 2026 after the county clerk forwarded the request (its metadata last synced 28 April 2022), kept as sent in mo/data/source/raw/cass-commission-districts/ and clipped to the county line in the same way. District 2 is the northwest of the county (Belton, Raymore and Peculiar) and District 1 the rest, as the county's own district map sent with it draws them.

Howard County — the shapefile of its two commission districts, the Western and Eastern Commissioner's Districts, that the county Assessor e-mailed to this project on 26 October 2026 after the county clerk was asked, kept as sent in mo/data/source/raw/howard-commission-districts/ and clipped to the county line in the same way. It stops at the Missouri River's bank, so the strip between the bank and the Census county line is split where the dividing line meets the river. The Secretary of State's Missouri Roster, linked here, lists its Assessor.

Wayne County — the map of its ten townships that the county clerk's office e-mailed to this project on 26 October 2026, with a red line marking the boundary between its Eastern and Western commission districts. The line runs along township lines only: Benton, Black River, Mill Spring and Williams lie west of it and the other six east. Drawn as the union of those townships' Census Bureau (TIGER) lines, clipped to the county line in the same way.

Dent County — the county clerk's office's list, e-mailed to this project on 26 October 2026, of the townships in each of its two commission districts: Current, Franklin, Gladden, Linn, Sinkin, Spring Creek East and Texas in the First District, and Meramec, Norman, Osage, Short Bend, Spring Creek West and Watkins in the Second. Drawn as the union of those townships' Census Bureau (TIGER) lines, clipped to the county line in the same way.

Ste. Genevieve County — a scanned page of the county's township and commissioner district map, e-mailed to this project by the county clerk's office on 27 October 2026, with its polling place list. The district line cuts through townships and precincts, so it was traced by hand from the scan and each district drawn as the Census Bureau's 2020 blocks on its side of the line, clipped to the county line in the same way; two short stretches hidden under printed labels were joined straight across, so near the line a block can be on the wrong side. The traced districts agree with the clerk's list of the seven precincts that lie whole in one district.

Cape Girardeau County — the county clerk's answer of 30 October 2026, that Commission District 1 is the City of Jackson and every unincorporated part of the county and Commission District 2 the City of Cape Girardeau with all its annexed land, with the precincts in each; the Second District is drawn from the City of Cape Girardeau's limits on the county's own map at SEMO GIS (CapeCo_PublicBase, Corp_Limit layer), and the First District is the rest of the county.

New Madrid County — the 'Commissioner Districts (May 2022)' map on the District Boundaries page of the county's website, a map of the Census Bureau's 2020 blocks by commissioner district, to which the county clerk pointed this project on 29 October 2026. Its district outlines were read out of the PDF and lined up with the county's blocks, and each district is drawn from the 2020 blocks the map puts in it; the blocks add up to the map's own populations, 9,429 and 7,005.

Audrain County — the county clerk's report of the commission district each election precinct votes in, e-mailed to this project on 28 October 2026, with her answers the same day that Jefferson Street divides Mexico precinct 3 (east side Eastern) and Route ZZ divides Community precinct (Prairie Township's side Eastern). Each district is drawn from the Census Bureau's 2020 blocks in its precincts; the one Community block east of Route ZZ was placed from where the road runs.

St. Clair County — a screenshot of the county's map viewer, e-mailed to this project by the county clerk's office on 28 October 2026, highlighting eight whole townships: Appleton, Butler, Center, Chalk Level, Jackson, Monegaw, Osage and Taber, the county's northern half, read as the Northern District, with the other eight townships as the Southern. The districts are drawn from the Census Bureau's township lines.

Saline County — the county clerk's list, sent to this project on 23 October 2026, of the townships and precincts in each of its two commission districts: Cambridge, Clay, Grand Pass and Miami townships and Marshall Wards 3 and 4 in the Northern District, and Arrow Rock, Blackwater, Elmwood, Liberty, Salt Fork and Salt Pond townships and Marshall Wards 1 and 2 in the Southern District, as the 2011 map sent with it also draws them. Drawn from the Census Bureau's (TIGER) township lines and, inside Marshall township, its 2020 voting districts Marshall 1 to 4, which tile that township; Marshall may have redrawn its wards since 2020.

Perry County — the Commissioner Districts layer of the county's public map at SEMO GIS (the Southeast Missouri Regional Planning Commission's map server, service PerryCo_PublicBase), read anonymously and clipped to the county line in the same way; the county clerk pointed to that map when asked on 2026-10-23. Whether it is the line the county's elections use today is not established either.

Iron County — the Commissioner District layer of the county's public map at SEMO GIS (service IronCo_Districts), read anonymously and clipped to the county line in the same way. No county office pointed to it; it was found on 2026-10-24 by reading the map server's folders. Whether it is the line the county's elections use today is not established.

Scott County — the Commissioner District layer of the county's public map at SEMO GIS (service ScottCo_Districts), read anonymously and clipped to the county line in the same way. No county office pointed to it; it was found on 2026-10-24 by reading the map server's folders. Whether it is the line the county's elections use today is not established.

layers.label: School District (Unified)

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 445 features for Missouri, measured 2026-10-21.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Missouri's school boards are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was read in this pass — recorded as gap mo-school-board-members.
source.applies: Missouri — every point outside the 71 elementary districts. The two tilings partition the state: their Census land areas sum to exactly the 115-county total (178,053 km2), measured 2026-10-21. TIGERweb's secondary tiling is empty for Missouri (0 features).

source.answers: The elementary school district covering the point, where the point is in one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 71 features for Missouri, measured 2026-10-21.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY — the same gap as the unified layer (mo-school-board-members).
source.applies: Missouri — the 71 elementary districts, 12,553 km2 of land between them. Everywhere else the unified card is the answer.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,040 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping Missouri, of the 1,977 in the state's own bounding box, in a mirrored tile archive (measured 2026-10-26); about 163 km2 of land on average for the 1,977, and ranked by them, which are what the map draws where the archive is not used (on the raster basemap); the layer hides outside Missouri

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='29'. 1,977 features in Missouri's box, measured 2026-10-21.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Missouri. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (Quincy, Illinois gives 62301 and Fort Scott, Kansas 66701, measured 2026-10-21).

layers.label: Township
layers.rank_note: 1,394 records tiling the state — 1,393 townships and the City of St. Louis, which the Census files as its own — about 128 km2 of land on average, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The township containing the point and its county, and whether the township has a government of its own.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 1,394 features for Missouri, measured 2026-10-21: 282 townships the Census records as active governments, in 20 counties; one, City township in Barton County, as a government partly consolidated with another; the 16 townships of Dade County as inactive; 1,094 townships with no government of their own; and the City of St. Louis, which the Census files as its own county subdivision because it belongs to no county.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. The 282 township governments elect their own officers, and no statewide roster of them was read in this pass — recorded as gap mo-township-officers. Every other township is a named area with no government of its own, so the card says the county governs it outside any city, town or village.
source.applies: Missouri — statewide, all 1,394 records. Whether a township has a government is read from the Census's own record of it (its functional status), so it cannot go stale against the name printed above it.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 947 incorporated places, about 8 km2 of land on average, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The city, town or village containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 947 features for Missouri (645 cities, 196 villages and 106 towns), measured 2026-10-21. The Census records 11 of them as inactive, and the card says so.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Missouri's cities, towns and villages elect their own officials, and no statewide roster of them was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap mo-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Missouri — statewide. A point outside every city, town and village is unincorporated, which the card states.

source.applies: Missouri — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Missouri State Capitol, 201 W. Capitol Avenue, Jefferson City, Cole County

negative_point.note: Franklin County, Kansas, near Ottawa, about 57 km west of the Missouri line — outside Missouri and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-21: TIGERweb's state and county layers name Kansas and Franklin County here (control: the State Capitol returns Missouri and Cole County), and none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it. MISSOURI HAS NO COAST, SO THIS POINT IS ON A NEIGHBOUR'S LAND AND WILL HAVE TO MOVE: Iowa, Illinois, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas and Oklahoma are live already, so Kansas and Nebraska are the only neighbours left, and the change that makes either one live moves this point to the other, the way Kentucky's go-live moved Indiana's.

geometry.note: The coverage ring for the wash (loadMetroOutline): the counties whose county commission district lines are drawn, dissolved from the same county fabric as mo-state-outline.json. It can be several disjoint parts.
The whole-Missouri outline (loadStateOutline), dissolved from the 115-county fabric: the wash's middle band and the ground the ZIP layer's coverage test reads.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside mo-state-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.
The 114 counties and the City of St. Louis — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 8 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119), the 2022 map, kept past 3 January 2027 because the 2026 election uses it.
The 34 Missouri Senate districts, from the state's own map of the 2022 plan.
The 163 Missouri House districts, from the state's own map of the 2022 plan.

The county commission districts of the 36 counties whose map viewer, download, posted township map, GIS office or clerk publishes or sends them (mo/scripts/build_mo_commission_districts.py), two per county, clipped to the Census Bureau's county lines.

rosters.note: U.S. House (MO) roster, refreshed weekly by update-mo-congress-roster.yml.
Missouri Senate roster from the Senate's own member pages, one record per seat, refreshed weekly. A vacant seat carries a record saying so, so the floor is the chamber's size.
Missouri House roster from the House's own published member list, on the same terms.

Every county's commission or council, county executive and other elected officers from the Secretary of State's Missouri Roster, one record for each of the 114 counties and the City of St. Louis, refreshed weekly by update-mo-county-officials.yml.

The 36 counties whose commission districts are drawn, by GEOID, with each district's 2020 census population, written by the same build as mo-commission-districts.json and held to it by its --check. The County Commission District layer's coverage test reads it beside state-counties.json, so a reader's first selection does not download the whole districts file.
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.
